text:
alex: Head's up — CI microbench on PR#15432 failed threshold. Sam's sampler timer test shows ~12% throughput drop.
ci-bot: job perf/microbench/sampler-timer — FAILED (threshold diff +12.4%)
helen: ugh, did the PR touch allocator/queue code?
alex: it only changed the quantized kernel selection logic, but the perf regression crops up in sampler-timer which shouldn't be touched.
sam: I ran the bench locally, reproduced on a dev GPU: attached flamegraphs. Link: https://internal.redwood/bench/15432/sampler-flame
maya: flamegraph shows bigger stack in `batch::alloc_lock` and `sampler::timer_wait` than baseline.
alex: here's the failing summary from CI:
```
--- baseline: 534.2 ops/s
+++ PR:       470.1 ops/s
delta: -12.02% (threshold -5%)
hot paths: batch::alloc_lock, kernel_selector::pick_best, sampler::timer_wait
```
helen: could be kernel selector now holding a global mutex during warmup path, leaking into sampler latency.
sam: to reproduce I ran `./run_microbench --seed 42 --warmup 100 --iters 1000` and saw same pattern.
alex: i'm going to bisect the merge window. last green commit on main before PR merged is `c3f9a2d`.
ci-bot: bisect job started (this may take ~30m)
maya: if that confirms selector change, we should revert the mutex change and land a follow-up to deconflict.
helen: also add a quick unit for sampler that asserts no global locks held during timer sleep. short-term guard.
sam: agreed. i'll prep a revert PR, label it `rollout-blocker` and ping infra.
alex: filing the revert now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/15481 — @helen @sam please review urgently :rotating_light:
deploy-bot: rollback plan created for PR 15432 -> 15481, notify on merge.
helen: once revert merges, we should re-run full perf pipeline and then re-land with lock-free warmup or finer-grained lock.
maya: note: impact only shows up under continuous batching + high sampler contention; add a targeted microbench in CI to catch this next time.
sam: adding that test now. tagging `perf/regression` and `ci-alerts`.
alex: thanks — keep updates in this thread, and cc @ops if we need emergency capacity to rerun benchmarks.
